title: APO Cod over Rice with Ginger-Shiitake Gravy
description: Combi-steamed cod sits on soft white rice under a glossy mushroom gravy finished with ginger and white miso.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with bottom drip pan, wire rack and food probe
Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: skinless Atlantic cod loin
ingredients.note: Weight after skin and pin bones are removed. Divide into two even portions about 3/4 to 1 inch thick. Fully thaw before cooking.

ingredients.name: fresh shiitake mushroom caps
ingredients.note: Weigh caps after trimming off the tough stems, then slice.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted plain meat-and-water broth without a vegetable blend.

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: Plain, unsalted and freshly cooked or promptly chilled.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the APO Gen 1 water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 230°F with sous vide mode off, 80% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 135°F.

steps.title: Soften the mushrooms
steps.text: Simmer {caps} and {ginger} with most of {broth} in the covered HexClad for 8–10 minutes until tender. Reserve a splash of broth for the rice.

steps.title: Warm the rice
steps.text: Heat {rice} with the reserved broth in the covered saucepan for 4–6 minutes, stirring once, until moist and at least 165°F throughout. Keep covered.

steps.title: Blend the mushroom broth
steps.text: Puree the mushroom mixture until smooth in the deep jug. Return it to the HexClad.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season the gravy
steps.text: Loosen {miso} with some warm gravy and whisk it back into the skillet with {sesame}. Keep warm over very low heat.

steps.title: Steam the cod
steps.text: Lay {fish} in the shallow pan on the middle APO rack with a spoonful of warm gravy over each loin. Insert the probe sideways into the thickest center. Cook for 7–16 minutes, checking from 6 minutes or when the probe signals. Pull each piece at 135°F after checking both centers.

steps.title: Rest under sauce
steps.text: Nestle the fish in the warm shiitake gravy off heat. Spoon sauce over the top, cover and rest for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Check carryover and doneness
steps.text: After resting, check each thickest center for about 140°F. Open a natural seam with a fork. The center should be opaque and separate easily into flakes. If either cue is unclear or the center is below 140°F, finish covered in hot sauce in the HexClad over low heat to a measured 145°F, checking every minute.

steps.title: Spoon into bowls
steps.text: Divide the soft rice between bowls, nestle the cod on top and ladle the shiitake gravy over the rice and through the cod flakes.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups of gravy for two in addition to the rice. Make ahead: Cook and chill the rice the previous day. The mushroom broth can also be blended a day ahead. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the cod, gravy and rice in a shallow portion for up to 1 month. Add a splash of water when warming the rice. Fridge reheat: Place a portion in a covered shallow pan with its sauce. Install the bottom drip pan and set the APO to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the probe target to 165°F and check from 10 minutes until the coldest center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw the covered portion in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge method. Option A uses ginger and toasted sesame oil. For gentler Option B, leave out the ginger and halve the sesame oil. The gravy is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 247 kcal, 29.5 g protein, 24.6 g total carbohydrate, 2.7 g fat, 1.5 g fiber, 212 mg sodium. Includes both the fish and its full share of sauce and any rice or potatoes listed. Sodium varies with the broth.
